counterfactual_missing_items: Leptomeningeal vascular malformation on MRI (absent; disconfirms Sturge-Weber syndrome)
Melanocytic facial lesion such as nevus of Ota (absent; would support oculodermal melanocytosis/phakomatosis pigmentovascularis)
Episcleral or conjunctival pigmentation (not described; would further support ocular melanocytosis)
decisive_items: Intraocular pressure measured by Icare tonometry was 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left.
Standard automated perimetry detected early visual-field defects in the right eye, and peripapillary OCT showed borderline retinal nerve-fibre-layer thickness on the right.
Topical latanoprost was initiated in the right eye, reducing intraocular pressure to 17 mm Hg.
response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that integrates the ipsilateral melanocytosis (iris heterochromia with micronodular elevations, trabecular hyperpigmentation, dark thickened choroid) with the secondary glaucoma (IOP 22 vs 12, visual-field defects, borderline RNFL, latanoprost response). R4 captures the melanocytosis but omits the glaucoma; R2 captures only the glaucoma; R3 is disfavored by absent leptomeningeal malformations and by the melanocytic rather than vascular/hemangioma pattern.

rejected.why: Glaucoma alone is incomplete; it ignores the underlying melanocytosis that explains the iris, angle, and choroidal findings.
Sturge-Weber syndrome is unlikely because MRI explicitly shows no leptomeningeal vascular malformations and the ocular findings are melanocytic rather than vascular/hemangiomatous.
